title: Heterogeneous probe orchestrator with adaptive failsafe for rollout quality
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an orchestrator that samples heterogeneous eval probes (golden prompts, customer-derived probes, and synthetic fuzz) during canary / shadow / A/B rollouts, computes a composite scorecard, and applies adaptive hysteresis-based gating with a graded failsafe that can: 1) throttle traffic, 2) divert to fallback model variant, or 3) open a human-review ticket and pause the rollout. The system must operate per-customer and per-cohort, respect privacy/PII constraints, and integrate with existing rollout conductor APIs.
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Spike completed to enumerate probe sources and latency budget impact (Ravi). Found avg additional p95 latency of 15ms when running local golden-set checks — within budget for most customers.

2025-02-25: Prototype sampler implemented that draws from three strata: golden-set anchors (10%), customer probes (50%), and synthetic diversity probes (40%). Initial sampling rate is configurable by cohort.
2025-02-27: Design review with Product & SRE. Agreed to keep default gating conservative (requires two-signal confirmation across separate metric families before auto-rollback).
2025-03-03: Instrumentation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-orchestrator/pull/412). Added tracing for per-probe latency and composite score computation.
decisions: Use stratified sampling instead of uniform sampling to ensure edge cases in synthetic probes are represented without overwhelming production traffic.
Composite score will be a weighted aggregation of: semantic-fidelity score (60%), token-accuracy/regression score (25%), and latency/availability penalty (15%). Weights are configurable per-project.
Auto-rollback requires at least two independent metric families to cross thresholds within a sliding window (default 5 minutes) to reduce false positives.
Human-in-loop escalation created when composite drop > 5% for more than 10 minutes despite throttling attempts.
tradeoffs: Aggressive gating reduces blast radius but increases time-to-ship and may cause unnecessary rollbacks for noisy metrics.
Richer probe sets improve detection coverage but increase cost and slightly increase p95 latency; we mitigate by running heavy-weight probes at lower sampling rates for low-tier customers.
Per-customer thresholds give better precision but add configuration complexity and require UI/console surfaces for SREs and customers to tune.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Alvarez): prefer conservative defaults and clear UI exposure for customers to opt-in to aggressive monitoring.
Design (Lena Ortiz): asked for a lightweight console view for probe coverage and recent probe traces; flagged accessibility for customer-managed private deployments.

SRE (Priya Singh): requested canary throttles be implementable as route policy changes so we can audit traffic shifts; recommended adding synthetic traffic replay capability for post-incident forensics.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler can select probes across three strata with per-cohort configurable rates and expose sampling metrics to tracing.
Composite score computed in real-time and stored per-request with an explanatory breakdown (semantic, token-accuracy, latency penalty) for debugging.
Policy engine supports three remediation actions: throttle, divert-to-fallback, pause-and-escalate; each action must be auditable and reversible.
Automated tests and chaos tests demonstrate rollback only occurs after two independent metric family failures within sliding window and not for single noisy drops.
Console view shows last 100 probe results, probe coverage heatmap, and allows SRE/PM to tune weights and thresholds for specific cohorts.
technical_design: Probe ingestion: lightweight agent in serving path annotates requests when sampled; heavy-weight probes run in parallel worker pool to avoid blocking main request path.
Score computation: streaming aggregation using existing metrics pipeline (Kafka -> Flink -> scoring service) with per-customer state kept in Redis for short-window hysteresis checks.
Policy engine: extension of rollout-conductor that accepts composite-scores and issues actions via existing route-control APIs; actions recorded to audit log and event bus.

Privacy: customer probes that may include PII are redacted at ingestion and evaluated in private-only mode for Private deployments; sampling rates default to 0 for sensitive customers until explicitly enabled.
Backfills: ability to run historical probe replays against a model snapshot for offline validation and to populate baseline distributions used by the gating logic.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary team): deploy sampler and scoring service to staging; validate with synthetic traffic and run unit/integration tests (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (internal alpha): enable for 5% of internal traffic on host orgs; monitor false-positive rate and cost impact (1 week).
Phase 2 (customer beta): opt-in for three trusted customers with different workloads; collect feedback and tune default weights/thresholds (2-3 weeks).
Phase 3 (gradual launch): default enabled for all new canaries with conservative sampling and gating (ramp over 4 weeks).
Rollback plan: ability to disable sampler via feature flag per-region; immediate mute route-level actions while preserving telemetry for post-mortem.
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary alerts: composite score regression alert when cohort-level composite drops > 3% with p-value < 0.01 over 3-minute window.
Secondary alerts: probe coverage drop (sampling pipeline backpressure), scoring latency > 50ms, worker pool saturation > 80%.
Pager: only trigger on confirmed auto-rollback events; all other alerts go to SRE channel with runbook link.
Dashboards: per-rollout drilldown showing recent probe samples, metric-family time series, and remediation actions taken.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy synthetic probes cause spurious rollbacks. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, two-signal confirmation, and lower sample rate for heavier probes.
Risk: cost of running large probe sets for many customers. Mitigation: tiered sampling defaults and admin throttle controls; offer opt-in premium monitoring add-on.
Risk: privacy/regulatory concerns for customer-derived probes. Mitigation: require explicit opt-in and apply redaction + private-only mode for sensitive customers.
Risk: complexity of per-customer configs leading to misconfiguration. Mitigation: provide sane defaults, validation checks in Console, and guardrails in policy engine.
